Category Panels Take Over the Awards Judging
By Bernard Tomlin, Members' Bulletin
For several years, every entry to the Alliance Awards was read by the same in-house committee at the association office. That committee now prepares the scoring guide only. Each award category is reviewed instead by a small group of people who put their names forward from member businesses. "A single committee could not read every entry with the care it deserved," said Yvette Bouchard, awards coordinator. "People who run a business judge these entries better than we did."

Late Shopping Evenings Draw Steady Crowds

By Janet Whelan, Local Business

Shops in central Havelock stayed open until 9:00 p.m. on two evenings last week, and the Havelock Retailers' Association reports steady visitor numbers.

"Thursday was busier than any Saturday this year, and most of those who came in had never visited us," said Arnold Deming, who runs a bookstore on Priory Lane.

The blocks did not open late on the evenings first announced. The South Block shops opened late on Wednesday, October 8, and the North Block on Thursday, October 9, the members having agreed to exchange the two dates.

The association, which meets on the last Tuesday of each month, has forty-one members, and thirty-four opened on one of the two evenings. Every participating shop appeared in a flyer delivered across the town, and the cost of printing and delivery was divided among them by storefront width. Officers say a further promotion is planned, but no date is fixed.
